verdict_context: REPLICATED (spot-check); descriptive assembly + annotation claims C1-C10 match, C11 (FadA count) PARTIAL, C12-C13 deferred

open_questions.q: Is the paper's count of 13 FadA paralogs biologically real, or does it inflate the family by folding in hemagglutinin-related sub-family members that a strict PF09403 domain scan would exclude?
open_questions.basis: Claim C11 is currently PARTIAL: paper reports 13 via RAST+InterPro+BLASTp; RefSeq PGAP strict product-name matching finds only 8. The 5-paralog gap is annotation-scheme dependent and unresolved in this replication. Fv113-g1's FadA repertoire is central to its proposed UC-mucosal-inflammation mechanism, so the true paralog count matters biologically, not just bookkeeping-wise.
next_steps: Run HMMER hmmsearch against Pfam PF09403 (FadA domain) on GCF_002356455.1 protein.faa with an explicit E-value / bit-score cutoff.
Build a curated FadA MSA from characterized F. nucleatum FadA/FadA2/FadA3 references and profile-search Fv113-g1's proteome.
Cross-check counts against the paper's Supplementary Table listing the 13 loci by locus tag and reconcile any that are labeled as fadA-like or hemagglutinin-associated.

open_questions.q: Does the D-MEM vs. BHI RNA-seq (DRA005507) actually show FDR<0.05 upregulation of the accessory T5SS and fadA paralogs, and is the effect size mechanistically plausible (log2FC magnitudes, replicate consistency)?
open_questions.basis: Claim C12 is the paper's core condition-dependent virulence hypothesis and is explicitly out of scope for this replication. It is the highest-value untested claim because the mucosal-inflammation model in UC hinges on it. Raw reads are public at DRA005507.
next_steps: Align to GCF_002356455.1 with HISAT2 or STAR, quantify with featureCounts against the RefSeq PGAP GFF.
Run DESeq2 with the paper's condition contrast; compare per-gene log2FC and adjusted p-values against the paper's supplementary DE table for the T5SS and fadA paralogs specifically.

open_questions.q: Do ISFv1 (~1.44 kb) and ISFv2 (~1.78 kb) actually contribute 47 and 48 insertions, and are those insertions preferentially located near virulence-factor loci (T5SS / fadA) as the mobile-element-driven expansion model would predict?
open_questions.basis: Claim C13 (IS-family enumeration) was deferred. If Fv113-g1's expanded virulence repertoire arose via IS-mediated duplication/mobilization, the spatial distribution of ISFv1/ISFv2 insertions should be non-random with respect to T5SS/fadA loci. Nothing in the current replication tests this.
next_steps: Run ISEScan or ISfinder on the closed chromosome plus both plasmids to independently catalog insertions.
Compare recovered family definitions and copy numbers against the paper's ISFv1/ISFv2 counts (47 and 48).
Compute a bedtools-based enrichment test: distance of each IS insertion to nearest annotated T5SS/fadA gene vs. a length-matched random null.

open_questions.q: Are the two plasmids pFV113-g1-1 (89.6 kb) and pFV113-g1-2 (68.1 kb) self-transmissible or mobilizable, and do they carry antibiotic-resistance or virulence-relevant cargo that could be horizontally transferred to other gut Fusobacteria?
open_questions.basis: The paper reports the replicon structure and GC of both plasmids (C3-C5, all MATCH) but the replication effort did not characterize plasmid gene content. If either plasmid carries a conjugative T4SS or a mobilization module, the mucosal-inflammation phenotype could spread horizontally to other F. varium or F. ulcerans strains in the same UC gut community, which changes the clinical picture materially.
next_steps: Extract each plasmid FASTA from GCF_002356455.1 and annotate with oriTfinder / MOBscan / CONJscan.
BLASTp each plasmid ORF against CARD (resistance genes) and VFDB (virulence factors).
Compare plasmid backbones against the F. ulcerans SB070 (GCF_037956035.1) already-staged comparator and any other Fusobacterium plasmid records in RefSeq.

open_questions.q: Is Fv113-g1's placement 'partially F. ulcerans-like' a robust phylogenetic signal, or an artefact of ortholog-overlap methodology (OrthoVenn) sensitive to comparator sampling and inclusion of accessory genes?
open_questions.basis: The paper positions Fv113-g1 as a notable F. varium subspecies with partial ortholog sharing with F. ulcerans, based on TBLASTx + FastTree + OrthoVenn against four F. varium comparators plus F. ulcerans. This replication did not re-run any orthology or phylogenetic analysis. The claim is central to how the isolate is taxonomically framed (subsp. designation vs. within-species accessory expansion), which in turn affects how comparative-genomics groups interpret future F. varium isolates from UC patients.
next_steps: Rerun OrthoFinder (modern replacement for OrthoVenn) across Fv113-g1, all publicly available F. varium complete/draft genomes, and multiple F. ulcerans references.
Compute an ANI (fastANI) and dDDH (Type Strain Genome Server) matrix for the same set to test the species/subspecies boundary quantitatively.
Reconstruct a core-genome phylogeny (Roary/PPanGGOLiN + IQ-TREE) and compare the placement of Fv113-g1 against the paper's FastTree topology.
